text: Which single-photon detector is now the most mature, reaching system detection efficiencies above 98%, timing jitter of a few to ~15 ps, and dark counts below 1 count per second?
choices: The silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) at room temperature
The pn photodiode operated in linear (non-avalanche) mode
explanation: SNSPDs deliver over 98% system detection efficiency, ~few to 15 ps jitter, and under 1 count per second dark counts; the chapter calls them the most mature component in quantum photonics (at the cost of 0.8-4 K operation). PMTs and SiPMs have far lower efficiency and higher noise at 1550 nm, and a plain photodiode in linear mode cannot resolve single photons.
